data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise 'used to' and 'would' for repeated past habits, with basic contrasts between past and present.
learningPoints: Use used to + base verb for past habits and past states that are no longer true.
Use would + base verb for repeated past actions when the past time is clear.
Do not use would for past states such as possession or identity.
Use didn't use to for negative past habits.
Use Did ... use to...? for questions.
Recognise when a sentence contrasts a past habit with the present.

sections.summary: Using 'used to' for a past habit.
sections.explain: USED TO + base verb describes a regular past habit that no longer happens.

words.word: I used to walk to school every day.
I use to walked to school every day.
I used walk to school every day.

sections.summary: Using 'used to' for a past state.
sections.explain: USED TO can describe a past state that is no longer true.

words.word: She used to live in London.
She would live in London.
She used to lived in London.

sections.summary: Using 'would' for a repeated past action.
sections.explain: WOULD can describe repeated past actions when the past context is clear.

words.word: Every summer, we would visit our grandparents.
Every summer, we would visited our grandparents.
Every summer, we would to visit our grandparents.

sections.explain: Use USED TO, not WOULD, for a past state such as having or being.

words.word: I used to have long hair.
I would have long hair.
I used to had long hair.

sections.summary: Making a negative with 'didn't use to'.
sections.explain: After DIDN'T, use USE TO, not USED TO, in careful standard writing.

words.word: He didn't use to like coffee.
He didn't used to like coffee.
He didn't use to liked coffee.

sections.explain: After DID, use USE TO + base verb.

words.word: Did you use to play tennis?
Did you used to play tennis?
Did you use to played tennis?

sections.summary: Using a base verb after 'used to'.
sections.explain: USED TO is followed by the base form of the verb.

words.word: We used to go there on Sundays.
We used to went there on Sundays.
We used to going there on Sundays.

sections.summary: Using 'would' in a clear past narrative.
sections.explain: WOULD works well for repeated actions after the past time has been established.

words.word: When I was a child, my father would read to me at night.
When I was a child, my father would reads to me at night.
When I was a child, my father would reading to me at night.

sections.summary: Contrasting a past habit with now.
sections.explain: USED TO commonly contrasts an old habit or situation with the present.

words.word: I used to drink tea, but now I prefer coffee.
I use to drink tea, but now I prefer coffee.
I used to drank tea, but now I prefer coffee.

sections.summary: Choosing 'used to' for a past situation.
sections.explain: USED TO is suitable for situations or states that changed.

words.word: There used to be a shop here.
There would be a shop here.
There use to be a shop here.
